svg.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: redo undo
svg.desc: Redo and undo. Redo records describe how to reapply a change, and rebuild committed work after a crash. Undo records describe how to reverse a change, and provide old versions for readers and rollback. InnoDB has both. Postgres has only redo, because old row versions stay in the table itself.
svg.text: Redo goes forward, undo goes back
Replayed after a crash, to rebuild committed work.
Used for rollback, and to give old snapshots an
InnoDB has both. Postgres has no undo log: old versions stay in the table until VACUUM removes them, so
rollback is free, and bloat is the cost.
